title: A launderer answers its sink's carrier, and only an idempotent escape answers a `string`
scope:
what the *return type* of a laundering `Core` member is, and the predicate that decides it;
`Core\Html::escape` answering `Core\Html\Markup`; `Core\Html::toSource` as the one reasoned way back to a
`string`; the return type `Core\Html::sanitize` will have when it lands. Not in scope: what makes a
parameter a sink, which is [0088 § 1](0088.md); the
`tainted` qualifier, its sources and its propagation, which are
[0024](0024.md); the terminal's substitution table, which is
[0086 § 1](0086.md); the HTML parser `sanitize` waits on, which is
[0122](0122.md).
dependsOnText:
[0024](0024.md) — § 3 is the rule this refines and
§ 5 is the sink that makes the refinement necessary.

summary.headline: Escaping for HTML returns markup, so a value is never escaped twice
summary.body:
`Core\Html::escape` returns `Core\Html\Markup`, not a `string`. An escaped value returned as
plain text looks like text nobody escaped, so a page that escapes automatically would escape it
again and `&` would arrive as `&amp;`. Markup is joined with `+`, refused by `.`, and placed
into a page as it stands, so a double escape is a compile error; `sanitize` returns markup for
the same reason. Every other cleaning function still returns a plain `string`, because you call
its sink by hand. `Core\Html::toSource` is the one way back, and it takes a written reason.
